items.name: Nintendo
clues: Founded in Kyoto, Japan, in 1889.
It started out making hand-painted playing cards.
In the 1960s it tried all sorts of things, including a taxi company and instant rice.
In 1989 it launched a small grey handheld machine, sold in many countries with a puzzle game of falling blocks.
It still makes playing cards in Japan, but most people know it for a console you can play on the TV or in your hands.
Its most famous character is a plumber with a moustache and a red cap.

items.name: IKEA
clues: Founded in 1943 in a farming area of southern Sweden, by a 17-year-old.
At first it sold pens, wallets, picture frames and nylon stockings by post.
In the late 1940s it started selling furniture, and in the 1950s it printed its first catalogue.
In 1956 an employee took the legs off a table so it would fit in his car. The company still tells this as the start of its most famous idea.
Today it has huge blue stores in dozens of countries, and some people only go for the meatballs.
Its name is the founder's initials plus the first letters of his family's farm and his home village.

items.name: Samsung
clues: Founded in 1938 in the city of Daegu.
It began as a small trading company selling dried fish, local groceries and noodles.
Over the next decades it went into sugar, textiles, insurance and shops.
In the late 1960s it moved into electronics. Its first product was a black-and-white TV.
Today it is one of the world's biggest makers of smartphones and memory chips.
Its name means “three stars” in Korean, and its phones are called Galaxy.

items.name: LEGO
clues: Founded in 1932 in a small town in Denmark, by a carpenter.
It began by making wooden toys such as ducks and yo-yos.
In 1949 it started making plastic bricks, and in 1958 it patented the design it still uses today.
In the early 2000s it had grown in too many directions and came close to bankruptcy, so it went back to basics.
Today it is one of the world's biggest toy companies, and in 2014 it had a hit film.
Its name comes from two Danish words meaning “play well”.

items.name: Peugeot
clues: Founded in 1810, when two brothers turned a family mill in eastern France into a steel works.
Its early products included saws and coffee grinders.
In the 1850s it made steel hoops for the huge crinoline skirts that were in fashion, and in 1874 its first pepper mill.
In the late 19th century it started making bicycles, and then cars.
Its pepper mills are still sold today, under the same name as the cars.
Its logo is a lion, and its car models have a zero in the middle of the number, like the 208 and the 3008.

items.name: Amazon
clues: Founded in 1994 in a garage near Seattle.
It started out selling books online.
Its founder almost called it Cadabra, but a lawyer said it sounded too much like “cadaver”.
In 2006 it started renting out computing power to other companies, and that is now one of its most profitable businesses.
Today it sells almost everything, streams films and series, and makes its own smart speakers.
It is named after the biggest river in South America, and its logo has an arrow from A to Z.
